title: Local H2 stabilization of positive subcritical steady Saint-Venant flow with positive friction by a single boundary PI controller with unit gate coefficient
source_title: PI controllers for the general Saint-Venant equations
author: Amaury Hayat
difficulty_reason: The short steady-input specialization is not the difficulty evidence and the source stability theorem is not supplied as a prerequisite. Sections2–3 construct coupled Riccati entropy weights and choose the integral-state boundary weight through a quadratic discriminant. The differentiated nonlinear entropy and Appendix norm/compatibility estimates then close H2 exponential decay for the actual PI boundary system, remaining substantive obligations after standard local hyperbolic well-posedness is allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Corollary1.8 restricted to constant positive inflow, positive friction k>0, positive-depth/positive-velocity subcritical smooth steady state on finite channel, C2 arbitrary slope and normalized unit gate coefficient v_G=1. Both exact authored gain alternatives1.22 retained, H2-compatible sufficiently small initial perturbations including integral controller state. Full new Riemann-coordinate/entropy/Riccati construction14–29, boundary inverseA30, identityD34–35, H2 functionalF36–37 and differentiated energyG37–41 read. Wang local quasilinear boundary wellposedness, ordinary Lyapunov continuation, Sobolev embedding and smooth ODE dependence are named prior foundations. Static selection makes time derivatives of target identically zero, so neither small-derivative dynamic target estimates nor their auxiliary proofs are needed. Positive k,V makes the strict positivity in Lemma3.2 supplied byD.1–D.3 valid; its frictionless generalization is excluded rather than repaired. v_G=1 keeps printed compatibility1.18 consistent with actual gate equation1.17 despite its missing v_G factor on integral terms. With static coefficients, a single fixed q from29 suffices; no assertion of a common q for time-varying boundary polynomials. Printed coercivity29 drops squared norms but statement2.17 and explicit functionalF fix the intended quadratic equivalence. Original static gate equilibrium shift is included via actual1.13–1.15 and authors12. No dynamic/feedforward/ISS variant or extra gain case counted as another unit.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: A Riccati supersolution supplies coupled interior entropy weights while a quadratic boundary discriminant selects the integral-state weight; the resulting nonlinear differentiated entropy controls two spatial derivatives and survives boundary compatibility.
